plan.title: Treated vs control lung DE with confounded-batch caveat
plan.analytical_narrative: The 12-sample lung dataset (6 treated, 6 control, salmon-derived raw integer counts, 12000 genes) has processing batch perfectly confounded with condition: all controls are B1, all treated are B2. This means no statistical method can separate a true treatment effect from a batch/technical effect from these data alone — the design matrix for condition+batch is not full rank, and any batch-correction tool (ComBat-seq, SVA, removeBatchEffect) would strip the condition signal along with the batch signal, or fabricate one. Per the grounded procedure (rule R-0005), the plan proceeds by fitting condition alone in DESeq2, but every downstream result is explicitly and irrevocably labeled as confounded — a candidate treatment signature that is equally consistent with a batch artifact. Track 1 does standard QC (to document, not fix, the confound: PCA/heatmap will show condition and batch as the same axis), pre-filtering, and DESeq2 Wald testing with apeglm shrinkage and BH-adjusted independent filtering. Track 2 takes the significant gene list forward to over-representation pathway analysis against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome (the enrichment method the knowledge service permits here, since a preranked GSEA default was flagged as not permitted for this confounded situation) using the tested-gene universe. The final report consolidates DE results, diagnostics, and enrichment, restating the confound caveat and recommending an unconfounded replication (batches spanning both conditions) before any biological or translational claim is drawn from this gene list.
